concepts.name: C0 baseline
concepts.what: Four lift rotors on twin booms for hover, a pusher on the pod for cruise.
concepts.note: C0 v0.3.1 as sized in analysis/results.json and placed in cad/params.txt: 17 in lift props on twin booms, H-tail on the booms, 14 in pusher on the pod, 2.4 m span in two 1.12 m panels.

concepts.name: Wingtip cruise propellers
concepts.what: Two cruise propellers at the wingtips, spinning against the tip vortex.
concepts.note: The pod pusher moves to two wingtip nacelles (14 in props shown). The disks reach past the wingtips.
concepts.claim: About 15 % less drag than a conventional layout at CL 0.5 (wind tunnel).

concepts.name: Boundary-layer-ingesting pusher
concepts.what: The pusher sits in the slow wake at the end of a long, tapered pod.
concepts.note: C0 already has its pusher at the pod tail. The BLI version stretches the boat-tail so the prop runs in the pod's wake; the published gains depend on how much wake it ingests.
concepts.claim: Up to 21.7 % less power than a tractor on a UAV; 3.95 % on a blended-wing body.

concepts.name: Aligned, faired stopped rotors
concepts.what: Two-blade lift props parked in line with the airflow, hubs faired.
concepts.note: Same airframe as C0. The CAD already draws the lift props parked fore-aft, but the BLHeli_S ESCs cannot park them (cad/README.md); this concept needs ESCs that can, plus hub fairings.
concepts.claim: Lowest stopped-rotor drag and asymmetry when blades align with the flow (CFD).

concepts.name: Tiltrotor
concepts.what: The front rotors tilt forward to give cruise thrust.
concepts.note: Front rotors tilt 90° and become the cruise propulsors; the pusher goes away. Two tilt mechanisms.
concepts.claim: Lightest option in a 5 kg UAV configuration comparison.

concepts.name: Blended wing with tilting motors
concepts.what: A tailless lifting body whose four motors tilt.
concepts.note: Tailless lifting body at the same 2.4 m span; all four motors tilt. Four tilt mechanisms.
concepts.claim: An open-source optimizer chose it over a quadplane.

concepts.name: Tiltwing
concepts.what: The whole wing rotates with its propellers.
concepts.note: Wing and four props pivot as one. Booms cannot hang off a tilting wing, so the tail moves to a tailboom with a small pitch fan.
concepts.claim: Negligible hover download, against about 25 % lift lost for a tiltrotor.
source: Oklahoma State tilt-wing proof of concept

concepts.name: Tailsitter
concepts.what: Stands on its tail to take off, then pitches 90° into wing-borne flight.
concepts.note: No tilt mechanism: the whole aircraft pitches 90° and stands on its tail fins to hover.
concepts.claim: Fewest parts of any VTOL; one 2024 variant needs a single actuator.

concepts.name: Box wing
concepts.what: Two wings joined at the tips into a closed loop; still lift + cruise.
concepts.note: Box wing on the C0 pod, booms, lift rotors and pusher; the tip fins close the loop and the H-tail goes away (fins stay on the booms).
concepts.claim: Beats a single wing at high lift and in gusts; loses at low lift coefficient.

concepts.name: Fan-in-wing
concepts.what: Lift fans buried inside a thick wing.
concepts.note: Two lift fans in a thick wing and a small tail fan, with the C0 pusher for cruise.
concepts.claim: No validated sizing method exists yet (thesis).

concepts.name: Cross-flow fan wing
concepts.what: A bladed drum along the wing makes both lift and thrust.
concepts.note: A bladed drum along each half-wing makes lift and thrust; no separate propellers.
concepts.claim: Very high lift at low speed (feasibility study).
